title: Sky Trial Sprint

selected_top_5.reasoning: The core play is repeated platform-to-platform jumping with gravity, landings, collision checks, and survival through increasingly difficult platform layouts.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: It is more abstract and score-driven than a traditional level-based platformer, but platforming is still the dominant mechanic.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The run has no explicit endpoint, the character moves automatically, difficulty escalates over time, and the structure is built around surviving for a higher score.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: The game scrolls vertically instead of forward horizontally, so it is a hybrid rather than a textbook endless runner.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The hero sweeps horizontally across the screen and the player times jumps to intercept safe landing spaces, creating a runner-like rhythm of committing to a path without free steering.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: There are no strict discrete lanes, so this is a loose fit based on movement feel rather than formal lane rules.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The visual identity strongly emphasizes neon glow, synth-like sci-fi presentation, and fast arcade motion, which matches the aesthetic and pacing implied by the category.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: This is partly an aesthetic match; mechanically it overlaps more strongly with platformer and endless runner categories.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The player goal is to stay alive as long as possible through escalating danger, with failure occurring from a single mistake that drops the hero below the camera.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: There is no resource survival or crafting loop, so this applies only in the arcade endurance sense.

uncertainty_notes: The game is best understood as a hybrid of vertical platformer and endless auto-runner.
Several other categories from the universe are weaker but adjacent, such as Speed runner or Obby runner.
Platformer game ranks highest because the collision, jumping, and landing loop is more mechanically central than the runner framing.
